svg.title: Return-to-work ledger after NATO's 2003 Iraq rupture
svg.desc: A documentary ledger showing the alliance's shift from the Turkey-defense dispute to renewed shared work in Afghanistan, support for Poland in Iraq, and Burns's repair rhetoric.
svg.text: The disagreement remained. So did the institution.

g.text: NATO authorizes defensive support for Turkey; the United States invades Iraq without NATO conducting the war as an alliance operation.
The policy dispute is not resolved by the Turkey compromise.
16 APR → 11 AUG 2003 · NATO TAKES ISAF COMMAND
At the request of Germany, the Netherlands and Canada, the alliance agrees to take strategic command, control and coordination of ISAF.
Germany—central to the February dispute—remains central to shared alliance work.
JUNE 2003 · SUPPORT FOR POLAND IN IRAQ
NATO agrees to help Poland with force generation, communications, logistics and movement for its stabilization role.
The alliance had not agreed to wage the Iraq war; it could still agree on bounded support afterward.

svg.text: Repair did not require anyone to pretend the Iraq dispute had been trivial. It required finding shared work that could still be done.
